title: Range-boundary breakouts are anti-predictive
gate_criterion: proceed only where |E[gross_r]| > 2 x cost_r per instrument-session
why_the_gate_exists: HYP-02 proposes inverting the strategy sign. Costs do not invert: if gross = -0.014 and cost = 0.076, the inverted strategy has gross = +0.014 and net = +0.014 - 0.076 = -0.062. The inversion makes things worse unless the GROSS edge is large enough to survive costs on both sides. The gate requirement |E[gross_r]| > 2 x cost_r ensures the magnitude of the gross signal exceeds the round-trip cost before inversion is arithmetic possible.

inversion_arithmetic.conclusion: Inverting a -0.014 R gross edge yields +0.014 R gross and -0.062 R net. The inversion makes the losing strategy less losing in gross, and more losing in net.

note_on_spec_observation: Review finding R4 correctly identifies that null_p_matched median = 0.978 means the median breakout entry underperforms random entry at matched stop distance. However (a) 'anti-predictive' implies fading yields a positive gross, which this arithmetic shows it does not; (b) the matched null exits at TIME 48% of the time (vs 12% for the breakout variant), so the null accumulates more of its return from not being stopped, not from a positive directional signal; (c) the gross signal is -0.014 R -- worse than the matched null that sits near zero, but not large enough in magnitude for inversion to help after costs.
spec_action: Close HYP-02 unrun. See docs/REVIEW_AND_HYPOTHESES.md HYP-02 §1 GATE: 'If gross is within noise of zero everywhere, HYP-02 is arithmetically dead and should be closed unrun.'
